name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP on one line after 8 Nov power cut
summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on a single power line after its 27th off-site power loss on 8 Nov; IAEA warns on winter grid
state: Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power for over 12 hours on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators (Ukrainska Pravda); it now relies on a single 330kV line (ANS, 19 Nov). IAEA Director General Grossi told the IAEA Board on 18 Nov that it would be difficult to overstate his concern about Ukraine's grid as winter sets in (ANS). Safety systems at other Ukrainian plants stayed operational, and no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release was found as of 22 Nov.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the UK. The IAEA's updates are the authoritative source on plant safety in Ukraine.
rubric_hit: Plant lost all off-site power 8 Nov; IAEA reports deteriorating grid safety = Watch

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
